clue.text: Endless kitty belonging to Douglas, possibly

definitions.text: Endless kitty belonging to Douglas, possibly

parts.words: Endless kitty belonging to Douglas, possibly
parts.note: a cat with no tail ('endless') from the island whose capital is Douglas

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cat that has lost its tail and might belong to a man called Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas looks like a person's name, but it is the capital of the Isle of Man, whose native breed of cat has no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man breed is famous for being tailless, and Douglas is the island's capital town.

clue.text: Travel south for such proposals?

parts.note: travel or movement is motion
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone at a meeting asks whether these ideas are suggestions to head south.
explanation.definitionFit: In a formal meeting, proposals put to the vote are called motions.

clue.text: Suit, cleaned, went astray in football club

indicators.note: going astray means the letters of the three words wander off into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer's suit, freshly cleaned, goes missing at the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' shuffles the letters of SUIT, CLEANED and WENT together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the English Premier League side based on Tyneside, nicknamed the Magpies.

clue.text: Saloon race bloomer?

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car, a sedan
a race or people is a nation

explanation.surface: A saloon car race goes badly wrong, a real blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, as in British slang, but here it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is something that blooms, so a garden pink grown for its blooms is a bloomer.

clue.text: Scraps for pets

explanation.surface: Leftover scraps are kept for the household animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are minor quarrels, and pets are fits of sulking, both names for petty squabbles.

clue.text: Dowries arranged for eccentrics

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Only oddballs would arrange marriages around dowries.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd people are eccentrics, informally called oddballs.

clue.text: Saw Widnes set out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone watched the town of Widnes set out on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WIDNES and SET together. Widnes is a town in Cheshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To have seen an event is to have observed it as an onlooker.

clue.text: Inappropriate for writer to turn up in Italy

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the abbreviation for Italy

parts.note: IT is the international abbreviation for Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word for a writer from bottom to top

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: It would be unsuitable for an author to show up in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses PEN to NEP, and 'in' puts it inside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsuitable or clumsy for the occasion is inept.

clue.text: But counting on the fingers is not part of its function

definitions.text: But counting on the fingers is not part of its function

parts.words: But counting on the fingers is not part of its function
parts.note: digit means both finger and numeral, so a machine named after digits does not count on fingers

explanation.surface: A remark that some calculator does not work by finger-counting.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke turns on digit meaning a finger as well as a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a machine computes with numbers in digital form, never with actual fingers.

clue.text: Difficult chores, with unknown amount of lively movement?

indicators.note: with here means holding the unknown letter inside the rearranged letters
difficult chores are troublesome, so the letters are worked into another order

parts.note: in algebra an unknown quantity is written as x, y or z

explanation.surface: Tough housework with no fixed end turns into a lively dance?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult' rearranges CHORES to SCHERO, and 'with' puts Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk, playful section of a symphony or sonata, often the third, is a scherzo.

clue.text: Stable person with a mighty tug?

explanation.surface: Someone describes a steady person who can pull really hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependable person is a pillar of support, and a boat that tows with great force is likewise a powerful tug.

clue.text: Seaman with an alias in Japanese port

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
aka, short for also known as, introduces an alias

explanation.surface: A sailor using a false name is found in a Japanese port.
explanation.definitionFit: A major port city on Honshu, Japan's main island.

clue.text: But it was not the organ of Addison's disease

definitions.text: But it was not the organ of Addison's disease

parts.words: But it was not the organ of Addison's disease
parts.note: Joseph Addison co-founded an 18th-century periodical; organ means a publication, not a body part afflicted by the illness named after another Addison

explanation.surface: A medical point about which body part Addison's disease affects.
explanation.walkthrough: Addison's disease affects the adrenal glands; but Joseph Addison, the essayist, ran a famous daily paper, and a paper is an 'organ'.
explanation.definitionFit: The periodical Addison and Steele founded in 1711 is the newspaper sense of organ.

clue.text: Established compositions for some planned team manoeuvres

parts.note: something established is set
musical or written compositions are pieces

explanation.surface: Established works are put to use for planned sports moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehearsed routines from free kicks or corners in football are such moves.

clue.text: Look out! It has high tars in it!

definitions.text: Look out! It has high tars in it!

parts.words: Look out! It has high tars in it!
parts.note: a lookout post high on a ship's mast with sailors (tars) up in it

explanation.surface: A warning about something containing high levels of tar.
explanation.walkthrough: Tars are sailors, and 'Look out' is the lookout platform high on the mast, not a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The lookout platform at the top of a sailing ship's mainmast holds a watching sailor.

clue.text: Artillery of colossal volume

indicators.note: of means the letters are taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: A huge volume of artillery fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A burst of artillery fired together is a salvo, a simultaneous discharge of guns.

clue.text: Irresponsible to be contented after smack

indicators.note: after places the word for contented following the word for smack

parts.note: a smack is a slap
contented means happy

explanation.surface: Someone is careless enough to feel pleased after a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual and careless in attitude; the term originally described a punch-drunk boxer.

clue.text: Pure carbon tip

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to tip is to lean

explanation.surface: Advice that pure carbon is a good tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsoiled or untainted things are spotless.

clue.text: Company clear off in light craft?

indicators.note: off means the letters are spoiled, put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A firm tells people to clear off in a small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round wicker boat used in Wales and Ireland is a lightweight vessel.

clue.text: Irregular player dismissed-he'll be omitted when the team is picked

definitions.text: he'll be omitted when the team is picked

parts.note: irregular means odd
a player is a man in a team
a dismissed batsman in cricket is out

explanation.surface: An erratic player is sacked and left out when the side is chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: The one left over after the others pair up or are selected is the extra one.

clue.text: Baggage point not used by writer

indicators.note: not used by means the point is dropped from the novelist's name

parts.note: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian novelist
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: An author leaves a piece of luggage unused at the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baggage' is an old disparaging word for a woman, not luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated insults for a woman thought to be immoral or slovenly.

clue.text: Athletes at university who never get firsts?

parts.note: runners are athletes
UP means at university, as in being up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Students on the track team who never earn first-class degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firsts' looks like top degrees, but means first places in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors who finish second or behind never take first prize.

clue.text: Muse of the dawn eating grass

indicators.note: eating means the word for dawn takes the informer inside it

parts.note: Eo- is the Greek-derived prefix meaning dawn, as in Eocene
a grass is an informer, a rat

explanation.surface: A goddess of the morning is seen grazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is British slang for an informer, the same as a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the nine Greek goddesses of the arts, presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Confirmation that piano takes topmost part

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
the roof is the top of a building

explanation.surface: Evidence that the piano is placed at the very top.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that settles a matter beyond doubt confirms it.

clue.text: Variety theatre's first half animal

indicators.note: first half keeps only the opening five letters of the ten in the theatre name

parts.note: a hippodrome was a music hall or variety theatre

explanation.surface: The first half of the show at a variety theatre features a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: British variety theatres were often called the Hippodrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African river mammal, informally shortened.

clue.text: Where one may find room for improvement in the country?

definitions.text: Where one may find room for improvement in the country?

parts.words: Where one may find room for improvement in the country?
parts.note: room for improvement suggests a ward where rural patients get better

explanation.surface: A question about where rural life could be bettered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'room for improvement' reads literally: a room where a patient improves, in a small rural hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rural infirmary serving a country district, with beds for recovering patients.

clue.text: The very last ambition nearly all followed

parts.note: an ambition or aim is an end
most means nearly all

explanation.surface: A last ambition is pursued by almost everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The furthest out or final in position is the one at the farthest end.

clue.text: Plant producing two kinds of carriage?

parts.note: a fly was a light hired carriage
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage

explanation.surface: Someone asks which works make two styles of coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory, but it is a carnivorous plant such as the Venus species.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect-catching vegetation like the Venus species snaps shut on its prey.
